Blonie Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Błonie, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Błonie from the 15th century, though the community only meaningfully developed after an 1862 settlement ban was lifted; by 1921, 1,262 Jews (24% of the town) were deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in 1941 and mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery was likely established in the second half of the 19th century. In summer 1940, Polish Army soldiers killed during the September 1939 campaign were exhumed from field graves and reburied here. A 1948 negotiation to trade synagogue-site management rights for cemetery fencing between Jewish and local authorities fell through unresolved. About 35 tombstones survived by 2011, but an unidentified vandal smashed all standing matzevot in spring 2013 - the destroyed pieces were secured in a police warehouse. Informational plaques about the cemetery and the 1939 soldiers' graves were installed in October 2013, and the European Jewish Cemeteries Initiative built a new fence in 2016.
